signals.signal: Board Member for Retail Dmytro Musienko: PrivatBank will buy 800 more ATMs in 2026, after 1,200 ATMs bought in 2025 for ~UAH 1bn; all fully-depreciated ATMs to be replaced by deposit-capable machines. Q1-2026 estate: 7,401 ATMs, 9,867 self-service terminals (PTKS), 1,053 branches, 345,390 POS (~60% of the UA POS market). ('ATM recycler' = a machine that takes deposited notes and re-dispenses them, so it needs far fewer cash-in-transit runs.)
signals.implies: Largest single ATM/recycler replacement pipeline in the Printec footprint outside the EU: NCR Atleos dispense/intelligent-deposit/recycling hardware, x-core multivendor ATM software, device telemetry & monitoring, APTRA OptiCash cash optimisation, plus managed/field services across 7,400+ units.
signals.likelihood: High - budget stated publicly and 2025 tranche already executed; procurement runs continuously through tender.privatbank.ua/Prozorro
signals.followup: Monitor tender.privatbank.ua and Prozorro for the 2026 ATM lots and their technical specs (deposit vs recycling); confirm incumbent hardware vendor mix.

signals.signal: Thales payShield 10000 HSM refresh for ATM/PTKS/POS continues: contract UAH 4,282,350 reported complete 26/06/2026 (PB-2026-05-07-3069339), preceded by EUR 282,450 (23/05/2026), EUR 199,630 (13/11/2025), UAH 11,125,380 (14/11/2025) and UAH 3,919,068 HSM technical support (26/11/2025). (An HSM is the tamper-proof crypto box that protects PIN and card keys.)
signals.implies: Direct hit on Printec's Thales HSM / PCI-PIN and remote key-injection line; a rolling multi-tranche refresh with repeat annual support contracts.
signals.likelihood: High - five separate HSM awards in 9 months, cadence roughly quarterly
signals.followup: Identify who supplied these payShield units and whether the support contract is renewed annually; approach for the next tranche and for remote key injection.

signals.signal: NBU Banking Sector Review, May 2026 (Q1-2026 data): the bank self-service device network (ATMs, deposit ATMs, PTKS) expanded for the THIRD consecutive quarter, driven by PTKS growth at individual private banks; the POS network kept growing, led in Q1 by private banks (+3.9k terminals) and state banks excl. PrivatBank (+1.1k). Branch count fell by 37 in Q1; 58 solvent banks remain after PIN Bank and Motor-Bank were declared insolvent in February 2026. Separately, Ukrainian banks cut 61 branches in H1-2026 to 4,754 branches at 01/07/2026.
signals.implies: Ukraine is one of the very few markets in the Printec footprint where the self-service estate is GROWING while branches shrink - the classic branch-to-self-service migration that drives recyclers, kiosks and multivendor ATM software.
signals.likelihood: High - three consecutive quarters of growth
signals.followup: Pull the next quarterly review (Aug-2026) for absolute device counts by bank group; identify WHICH private banks are adding PTKS.

signals.entity: National Bank of Ukraine / Power Banking
signals.signal: Power Banking - the NBU-coordinated joint network of bank branches that keeps working during blackouts - has grown to ~2,396-2,400 branches, close to 55% of all Ukrainian bank branches; ~75% of them belong to systemically important banks. Branches run on generators/alternative power with backup comms (incl. Starlink), reinforced cash collection, and most offer inter-bank 'ATM national roaming' (a customer of any participating bank can use any participating bank's ATM). Ukrgasbank has joined the network.
signals.implies: Resilience is a hard procurement driver here rather than a compliance box: physical ATM security, UPS/power-tolerant self-service hardware, device telemetry that reports availability across a shared network, and cash-optimisation to keep autonomous branches stocked. [STANDING programme - dated 2022, but the branch count and Ukrgasbank accession are the recent movement.]
signals.likelihood: High - network is operational and still expanding
signals.followup: Get the current official count and participating-bank list from power.bank.gov.ua (403 to fetch tool - operator/browser needed); position ATM telemetry as the roaming-availability layer.

signals.signal: NBU approved the 2026 bank resilience assessment - asset-quality review by independent auditors plus stress testing under baseline and adverse macro scenarios, covering 26 banks that hold more than 90% of banking-system assets; the NBU published the stress-testing methodology for the largest banks in Q1-2026. The NBU also approved the list of 16 systemically important banks for 2026 by Board decision of 11/06/2026 (Kredobank, OTP, Oschadbank, Pivdennyi, PrivatBank, PUMB, Raiffeisen, Sens Bank, Taskombank, Ukrgasbank, Ukreximbank, UkrSibbank, Universal Bank among them). Separately the NBU is developing 'financially inclusive banks' - limited-licence institutions that post offices and retail chains could operate in frontline regions.
signals.implies: Supervisory pressure on operational and data capability at the 26 largest banks (risk data, reporting, controls) plus a brand-new agent-banking/limited-licence channel that would need low-cost self-service kiosks, eKYC/e-signature onboarding and remote key management to serve frontline areas.
signals.likelihood: Medium - the inclusive-bank concept is at development stage
signals.followup: Find the NBU primary resolution text for the 2026 resilience assessment and any consultation paper on 'financially inclusive banks' on bank.gov.ua (retry with desktop UA); this is the eKYC/kiosk lead.
